config.title: Responsive typography (clamp)

intro.title: Responsive typography (clamp)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with text that automatically adjusts its size based on the screen width, using responsive typography. You will learn the core concept of the CSS `clamp()` function, which allows you to set a minimum, preferred, and maximum font size in one line. The main technologies involved are CSS and the `clamp()` function. By the end, you'll understand how to create fluid, readable text that works on both mobile and desktop screens.
intro.usecase: Responsive typography with clamp() is essential for creating fluid text that adapts seamlessly across devices in modern web applications. You'll use this technique in product dashboards where headings and metrics need to scale appropriately from desktop monitors to mobile screens. It's also crucial for marketing websites with hero sections, where taglines must remain readable on all viewports, and in e-commerce product listings where item titles and prices require consistent legibility. This approach eliminates the need for multiple media queries for text sizing, making your CSS more maintainable while ensuring optimal readability across the entire device spectrum.

objectives: Implement the clamp() function to define responsive font sizes in CSS
Configure the minimum, preferred, and maximum values for typographic scaling
Apply clamp() to different text elements like headings and paragraphs
Manipulate viewport units within clamp() to control scaling behavior
Integrate clamp() with existing CSS properties like line-height and font-weight
Construct a complete responsive typography system using clamp()
Update static font-size declarations to responsive clamp() alternatives

steps.title: Set up the HTML structure for typography examples
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a basic structure containing a heading and a paragraph that we'll target with CSS for responsive typography.
steps.hint: Start with the standard HTML5 doctype and include a heading and paragraph inside the body.
steps.analogousExample:
Welcome to Responsive Typography

This paragraph will demonstrate responsive text sizing.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Responsive Typography</title>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add a heading and paragraph here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: An HTML file is created with a heading and paragraph element ready for CSS styling.
successCriteria: The HTML file includes a heading (h1) and a paragraph (p) element inside the body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both a heading and a paragraph element inside the body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure is incomplete. Please create a heading and a paragraph element inside the body.

steps.title: Add basic CSS styling for text elements
steps.instruction: Add a
steps.hint: Place the <style> tags after the <title> element. Inside, write CSS selectors for h1 and p with the specified properties.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Responsive Typography</title>
    <!-- Add a <style> block here with CSS for h1 and p -->
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add a heading and paragraph here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML file now contains a <style> block with CSS rules that set basic typography styles for headings and paragraphs.
successCriteria: A <style> block exists in the <head> with CSS rules for h1 (font-size: 2rem, color: #333) and p (font-size: 1rem, color: #666).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure both h1 and p elements have the specified font-size and color properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The <style> block or CSS rules are missing or incorrect. Check that you've added the <style> tags with the correct selectors and properties.

steps.title: Introduce the viewport meta tag for responsive design
steps.instruction: Add a viewport meta tag inside the <head> section to enable responsive scaling on mobile devices.
steps.hint: The meta tag should have name="viewport" and content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0". Place it before the <title> tag.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example meta tag for responsive design -->
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <!-- Add the viewport meta tag here -->
    <title>Responsive Typography</title>
    <!-- Add a <style> block here with CSS for h1 and p -->
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add a heading and paragraph here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML head section now includes a viewport meta tag, which is essential for responsive typography to work correctly on mobile devices.
successCriteria: A meta tag with name="viewport" and content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" is added to the <head> section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a meta tag, but check the attributes. It needs name="viewport" and content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0".
steps.feedbackWrong: The viewport meta tag is missing or incorrect. Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"> inside the <head>.

steps.title: Create a fixed font size for comparison
steps.instruction: Inside the existing <style> block, add a CSS rule for the h1 element that sets its font-size to a fixed value of 32px.
steps.hint: You can add a CSS rule like 'h1 { font-size: 32px; }' within the <style> block to apply a fixed font size to the heading.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Similar: setting a fixed font size for a paragraph */
p { font-size: 16px; }
steps.seedCode:
Responsive Typography Example

This paragraph will demonstrate responsive font sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h1 heading will have a fixed font size of 32px, which will not adjust based on screen size.
successCriteria: The h1 element has a CSS rule setting font-size to 32px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're setting the font-size property specifically for the h1 element with a value of 32px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 element doesn't have a fixed font size of 32px. Check that you've added a CSS rule for h1 with font-size: 32px; inside the <style> block.

steps.title: Introduce responsive units with viewport width (vw)
steps.instruction: In the h1 CSS rule, replace the fixed font-size value with a responsive value using viewport width units (vw).
steps.hint: Use vw units to make the font size scale with the viewport width. For example, 5vw means 5% of the viewport width.
steps.seedCode:
Responsive Typography Example

This paragraph will demonstrate responsive font sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h1 heading will now have a font size that scales proportionally with the viewport width.
successCriteria: The h1 CSS rule uses vw units for font-size
The fixed px value has been replaced with a vw value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using vw units (like 5vw) instead of px or other fixed units.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 font-size should use vw units (viewport width) to create responsive typography. Try replacing the fixed px value with something like 5vw.

steps.title: Identify the lesson with unbounded scaling
steps.instruction: Replace the fixed font-size in the h1 selector with a viewport width unit (vw) to see how text scales at different screen sizes.
steps.hint: Use a value like 5vw for font-size to make the heading responsive to viewport width.
steps.seedCode:
Responsive Typography Example

This paragraph will demonstrate responsive font sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The heading text will now scale with the viewport width, becoming very small on narrow screens and very large on wide screens.
successCriteria: The h1 selector uses a vw unit for font-size instead of a fixed px value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to replace the entire font-size value with a vw unit (like 5vw).
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 selector should use a vw unit for font-size. Try replacing 32px with a value like 5vw.

steps.title: Introduce the clamp() function syntax
steps.instruction: In the CSS for the h1 selector, replace the fixed font-size value with a clamp() function that has three parameters: a minimum value, a preferred value, and a maximum value. Use 24px as the minimum, 5vw as the preferred, and 48px as the maximum.
steps.hint: The clamp() function syntax is clamp(min, preferred, max). Place it where the font-size value goes.
steps.seedCode:
Responsive Typography Example

This paragraph will demonstrate responsive font sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h1 font-size will use clamp(24px, 5vw, 48px) instead of a fixed pixel value.
successCriteria: The h1 selector's font-size property is set to clamp(24px, 5vw, 48px).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the clamp() function with exactly three values: minimum, preferred, and maximum.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clamp() function wasn't implemented correctly. Check the syntax: clamp(min, preferred, max).

steps.title: Apply clamp() to create responsive typography
steps.instruction: Replace the fixed 32px font-size value in the h1 selector with a clamp() function that sets a minimum of 1.5rem, a preferred value of 5vw, and a maximum of 3rem.
steps.hint: The clamp() function takes three values: minimum, preferred, and maximum. Use rem units for the min/max bounds and vw for the fluid scaling.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example of clamp() for responsive padding */
padding: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 2rem);
steps.seedCode:
Responsive Typography Example

This paragraph will demonstrate responsive font sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h1 heading will now scale fluidly between 1.5rem and 3rem based on viewport width, using 5vw as the preferred scaling value.
successCriteria: The h1 selector uses a clamp() function with 1.5rem as minimum, 5vw as preferred value, and 3rem as maximum.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your clamp() syntax. Make sure you have three values separated by commas: minimum, preferred, and maximum.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 still uses a fixed font-size. Replace the 32px value with a clamp() function containing three values: minimum, preferred, and maximum.

steps.title: Test the responsive typography at different screen sizes
steps.instruction: Resize the browser window to test how the clamp() function behaves at mobile, tablet, and desktop screen sizes.
steps.hint: Drag the browser window edges to make it narrower (like a mobile device) and wider (like a desktop). Observe how the heading font size changes smoothly but stays within the min and max bounds you set.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Testing responsive behavior by resizing viewport */
/* The font-size should scale between 20px and 48px as the viewport width changes */
steps.seedCode:
Responsive Typography Example

This paragraph will demonstrate responsive font sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll see the heading font size adjust fluidly as you resize the window, but it will never go below the minimum or above the maximum values you specified in the clamp() function.
successCriteria: The clamp() function is working correctly if the font size scales responsively while staying within reasonable bounds at all screen sizes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you resize the window enough to see the font size change - try very narrow (mobile) and very wide (desktop) sizes to observe the full range.
steps.feedbackWrong: The testing didn't work as expected. Make sure you have the clamp() function properly applied to the h1 element and that you're resizing the actual browser window to see the responsive behavior.

steps.title: Apply clamp() to multiple text elements
steps.instruction: Add a clamp() function to the paragraph's font-size property to create responsive typography for the paragraph text.
steps.hint: Use the clamp() function with appropriate minimum, preferred, and maximum values for paragraph text. For example, clamp(16px, 2vw, 20px).
steps.seedCode:
Responsive Typography Example

This paragraph will demonstrate responsive font sizing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph text will have responsive font sizing that scales smoothly between minimum and maximum values based on viewport width.
successCriteria: The paragraph selector has a font-size property using the clamp() function with appropriate values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the clamp() function correctly. Check that you have all three parameters: minimum value, preferred value (usually in vw), and maximum value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph doesn't have a clamp() function applied. Remember to use the clamp() function syntax: clamp(min, preferred, max) where preferred is typically a viewport-based unit like vw.
